clue.text: Defect in the hose that's used by firemen

definitions.meaning: a run in a stocking or pair of tights, where a column of stitches unravels
the extending climbing frame of rungs carried on a fire engine

explanation.surface: A complaint about a flaw in some hosiery, or in the firefighters' hose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hose' tempts you towards the firemen's water pipe, but here it means stockings; the run in them is the first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are everyday nouns: a laddered stocking has a vertical run, and firefighters climb an extending set of rungs.

clue.text: Kill dead, accepting one pound for it

indicators.note: something that accepts takes another thing in, so the word for dead holds the rest

parts.note: late means deceased, as in 'the late king'
one is the Roman numeral I
quid is British slang for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: A hitman agrees to murder someone for a single pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dead' looks like part of the killing, but it is the container; 'accepting' signals the insertion and 'for it' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To liquidate a person is to eliminate or murder them.

clue.text: There's no catch in it

parts.note: 'catch' read as a haul of fish rather than a hidden snag: a body of water too salty for fish

explanation.walkthrough: 'No catch' sounds like a deal without a hidden drawback; here it means no fish to be caught.
explanation.definitionFit: This salt lake between Israel and Jordan is so saline that fish cannot live in it.

clue.text: No head on beer? That is strange

indicators.note: the top of the drink is missing, so its first letter is taken off

parts.note: taken as the word itself before losing its first letter
i.e. abbreviates id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A drinker notices a pint has no froth on it and finds that odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like froth on the pint, but it is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means weird or uncanny, so odd in an unsettling way.

clue.text: Venomous creature in one box carried by musician

indicators.note: something carried is held within the carrier, so these words go inside the musician's word

parts.note: a piper is a musician who plays the bagpipes
one is the Roman numeral I
box is informal for a television set, TV

explanation.surface: A snake travelling in a single crate, transported by a snake-charming player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' looks like a crate for transporting the snake, but it is slang for a television; 'carried by' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a family of snakes, such as rattlesnakes, with heat-sensing pits and a poisonous bite.

clue.text: In which the innocent align themselves with the guilty

definitions.text: In which the innocent align themselves with the guilty

parts.words: In which the innocent align themselves with the guilty
parts.note: 'align' read literally as standing in a line beside a suspect, not taking sides with wrongdoers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Align themselves with' suggests siding with criminals; at the police station it means standing in the row.
explanation.definitionFit: Witnesses pick a suspect from a police line-up of innocent volunteers.

clue.text: Cite devil showing unusual disposition to wit

indicators.note: disposition read as arrangement: the letters are laid out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Name the devil for being in a strange mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposition' suggests temperament, but it means arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word, abbreviated viz., means namely, introducing an example.

clue.text: South American girl's study

parts.note: Peru is a South American country
Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally or Sarah; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A young woman from South America has her own room for working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'study' looks like a room (the girl's study), but it is the noun for a careful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A perusal is a careful reading or examination of something.

clue.text: Added recommendation for a jockey

definitions.meaning: an extra clause attached to a verdict or report, such as a jury's recommendation

explanation.walkthrough: 'for a' only links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers a supplementary clause on a document and a person on horseback.

clue.text: Young drinkers may seek desperate remedies

definitions.text: Young drinkers may seek desperate remedies

parts.words: Young drinkers may seek desperate remedies
parts.note: children drinking through tubes grab for their drinking straws, while the idiom means trying anything in desperation

explanation.walkthrough: The literal picture is children reaching for drinking straws; the idiom means making a desperate attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to try any hope, however slight, when in trouble.

clue.text: Dance seen as being exercise by English

parts.note: qua is Latin used in English for 'in the capacity of', 'as being'
drill is repeated practice or military exercise

explanation.surface: A remark that a dance can be thought of as a kind of English workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen' and 'by' are only link words joining the definition and the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a square dance for four couples, popular in eighteenth- and nineteenth-century ballrooms.

clue.text: Risked a little money once with a bet on roulette

parts.note: D was the abbreviation for the old British penny, before decimal coinage in 1971
red is one of the colour bets on a roulette wheel

explanation.surface: A gambler recalls staking a small old coin on the roulette table.
explanation.walkthrough: The old penny (abbreviated d, from Latin denarius) was the smallest everyday British coin before 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: To have dared is to have ventured or had the nerve to chance something.

clue.text: Problem children

definitions.meaning: a matter in dispute or a point of concern

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers a point of contention and, in legal language, a person's descendants.

clue.text: Better system Aristotle developed

indicators.note: the letters are worked up into a new form, so the philosopher's name is rearranged

explanation.surface: A claim that the ancient Greek philosopher devised a superior method of thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like the comparative of good, but it means a person who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A tote machine that pools wagers and computes payouts is a system for gamblers.

clue.text: A number of people about to go into the theatre

definitions.text: A number of people about to go into the theatre

parts.words: A number of people about to go into the theatre
parts.note: 'number' read as something that numbs, used on patients about to enter an operating theatre, not an audience entering a playhouse

explanation.walkthrough: The clue paints a crowd heading into a playhouse; read 'number' as numb-er and 'theatre' as the operating room.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug given before surgery numbs a patient so the operation is painless.

clue.text: She cleans out for the steward

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A housekeeper tidies up on behalf of the manager.
explanation.walkthrough: The page reads 'cleans': SHE CLEANS rearranged ('out').
explanation.definitionFit: A seneschal was the steward who managed a medieval noble household.

clue.text: A large number of Indians dont have enough, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken, so the entry sounds like the word for being short of something

parts.note: to lack something is to be without enough of it

explanation.surface: Many people in India are said to be going without.
explanation.walkthrough: A lac (or lakh) is the Indian word for one hundred thousand, used especially of people or rupees.
explanation.definitionFit: In South Asian usage the term denotes a hundred thousand, so a great crowd of people.

clue.text: New or ancient vessel

indicators.note: new signals a fresh form of the words that follow, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question of whether a ship or pot is modern or old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like part of a choice of ages, but it is the anagram signal for OR ANCIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel in the sense of a receptacle, such as a jar or box.

clue.text: Easily-led females alternating directions

definitions.note: plural in the clue, while the entry is the singular noun; read as a type of animal

parts.note: compass points east, west, east, swapping back and forth: E, W and E
compass points east, west, east, swapping back and forth: E, W and E
compass points east, west, east, swapping back and forth: E, W and E

explanation.surface: Docile women keep switching which way they head.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass points alternate: east, then west, then east again.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sheep, and sheep are proverbially meek followers of the flock.

clue.text: Representative contributed to capital raised for ruler

indicators.note: in a down entry raising something lifts it upwards, so it is read bottom to top
the piece contributed goes into the other, so it sits inside the city

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: A delegate gave to a fund being raised for the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' looks like fundraising, but in a down clue it turns the whole assembly upwards; 'contributed to' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is the supreme ruler of an empire.

clue.text: Inferior to a particular area, impractical to enclose

indicators.note: one piece encloses another by going round it, so the impractical phrase surrounds the rest

parts.note: 'not on' is British colloquial for unacceptable or not feasible
a patch is a particular small area, as of ground

explanation.surface: A grumble that some district is second-rate and too unwieldy to fence in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on' is British slang for out of the question; 'to enclose' signals that it goes round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means nowhere near as good as something else, so worse than it.

clue.text: Where one lives a little in Panama, say

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a Panama is a type of straw hat
a bit is a little

explanation.surface: Describing one's home as a small spot in Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panama' looks like the country, but it is the straw hat, given by example ('say').
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural home or environment of an animal or plant.

clue.text: He many take an interest in banking

definitions.text: He many take an interest in banking

parts.words: He many take an interest in banking
parts.note: a person who puts money in a bank earns interest on it, rather than finding the trade of banking interesting

explanation.walkthrough: 'many' is a misprint on the page for 'may'. 'Take an interest' suggests curiosity, but means receiving interest payments.
explanation.definitionFit: A customer who places funds in an account is paid interest by the bank.

clue.text: Material that's dug up

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: mined means dug out of the ground

explanation.surface: Fabric unearthed in an excavation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a hard-wearing cotton cloth used for jeans.

clue.text: Firm support for a hooded killer

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A company sponsoring a masked assassin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word; the hood is the snake's flared neck, not an assassin's mask.
explanation.definitionFit: This venomous snake spreads a flap of skin round its neck when threatened.

clue.text: Thrash about the ring showing little craft

indicators.note: about means going round, so the beating word surrounds the ring

parts.note: to cane is to thrash with a stick
the ring-shaped letter O

explanation.surface: Flailing round the boxing ring displays little skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like skill, but it is a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoe is a small, light boat paddled by hand.

clue.text: Former PM on top of the world apparently --

definitions.meaning: Lord ... was British Prime Minister 1770-1782, during the American War of Independence

definitions.text: on top of the world apparently
definitions.meaning: the direction at the top of a conventional map or globe

explanation.walkthrough: The dash leads into the next clue, which names another prime minister. 'On top of the world' suggests elation, but here is map orientation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Georgian prime minister bore this title, and it is the compass direction placed uppermost on maps.

clue.text: -. and another is putting on weight

parts.note: adding means putting on, as of extra pounds
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a second statesman is getting fat.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots carry on from the clue before, so 'another' means another former PM: Henry Addington, Prime Minister 1801-1804.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Addington was a British Prime Minister after Pitt, so another holder of the office.

clue.text: He wants to raise people's standard of living

definitions.text: He wants to raise people's standard of living

parts.words: He wants to raise people's standard of living
parts.note: 'standard of living' read as the ethical quality of how people behave, not their material wealth

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase sounds like economics, but the person here wants better conduct, not higher incomes.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a person preaches about right and wrong, trying to improve others' ethics.

clue.text: Hector — a good man to look out for

indicators.note: the looking word stretches out round the other piece, so it is placed outside

parts.note: to peer is to look closely
St, for saint, is the crossword stand-in for a good man

explanation.surface: Advice that a hero of Troy is a fine fellow worth watching out for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hector' looks like the Trojan prince, but as a verb it means to bully; 'out' signals one piece placed round the other, and 'a', 'to' and 'for' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To hector someone is to harass or nag them, a close synonym.
